finding.summary: Test named "does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it" never exercises a rejection, so it cannot fail if the `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` guard is removed
finding.evidence: The test hits `/callback?code=unbound` with no `state`. In login.ts:306-317 that branch writes a 400 and returns — it never calls `callbackReject`, and `settled` stays false. The only path that rejects `callbackPromise` is the 30s timeout (login.ts:373-385), which this test never triggers (it waits 50 ms and asserts the promise is still pending). So the pre-attached `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` added at login.ts:259 — the whole behavior the test's comment claims to protect ("a rejection raised in that window must not surface as an unhandled rejection") — is never exercised. Deleting line 259 leaves this test green. There are no fake timers anywhere in the file (no `vi.useFakeTimers`), so no other test covers it either.

verdict.reason: Neither the test nor the code the finding describes exists in this repository. (1) No file `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` — a repo-wide glob for `**/login-callback*` returns nothing. (2) No test named "does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it" exists anywhere; repo-wide greps for that phrase, "awaits it", and "arrives before" match no test file, and enumerating all 34 `it(...)` blocks in login.test.ts shows no such test. (3) The `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` guard supposedly "added at login.ts:259" does not exist: a repo-wide grep for `callbackPromise` yields only login.ts:538 (Promise constructor), 639 (a prose comment), and 669 (`waitForCallback: () => callbackPromise`). There is no `.catch(() => {})` in the file; line 259 is prose inside a comment about printing the OAuth URL. (4) The cited line ranges point at unrelated code — login.ts:306-317 is workspace-selection prompt logic, 373-385 is the tail of `nonceMatches` plus the CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS doc comment; the real state refusal is at 578-586 and the real timeout at 656-666. (5) The actual design is the inverse of the finding's premise: the timer is armed inside the listen callback (642, 656-666) precisely to avoid an unawaited rejection, and the real test for that behavior, login-listen-failure.test.ts:49-64, is non-vacuous — it registers a real `process.on('unhandledRejection')` handler (53), uses a real `timeoutMs: 50` (56), waits 200 ms so the timer would fire if still armed (61), and asserts no unhandled rejections (63). Fake timers are unnecessary because a short real timeout is used, so the finding's "no vi.useFakeTimers anywhere" argument does not establish a gap.

finding.summary: No test covers the `login` action body: nonce minting, `--allow-unbound-callback` wiring into `startCallbackServer`, or that `open()`/stderr receive `startUrl` rather than the nonce-carrying authorize URL
finding.evidence: The only test of the command is `registerLoginCommand` → `expect(login?.options.map(o => o.long)).toContain('--allow-unbound-callback')`, which asserts the option exists but nothing about its effect. The action (login.ts:22-83) is where `randomBytes(32)` is minted, `allowUnbound: localOpts.allowUnboundCallback === true` is passed, `setAuthorizeUrl(buildAuthorizeUrl(...))` is called and `open(startUrl)`/`console.error(startUrl)` happen. If the action passed `state` to `open()` (the leak this change exists to prevent), or wired the flag to the wrong option name (commander camel-casing), every test in the file would still pass, because they all call `startCallbackServer`/`buildAuthorizeUrl` directly with hand-built arguments. Searched packages/cli/test for `allowUnbound`, `open(`, `startUrl` — only helper-level uses.

verdict.reason:
The finding's premises do not hold in this tree. There is no `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts` contains no `startUrl`, `buildAuthorizeUrl`, or `setAuthorizeUrl` — the action delegates to an exported, dependency-injected `runLogin` (login.ts:207-291) with a `LoginDeps` seam (login.ts:188-205). Two separate test files exercise exactly the behaviors said to be untested:

1. `packages/cli/test/login.test.ts:463-566` drives the real `runLogin` with injected deps and asserts: the nonce handed to `startCallbackServer` is the same one placed in the OAuth URL (`login.test.ts:519-534`), a fresh nonce/verifier per login, i.e. nonce minting (`:548-553`), and the `--allow-unbound-callback` wiring in both states — `expect(listenerOptions?.allowUnbound).toBe(false)` by default (`:555-558`) and `.toBe(true)` when `allowUnboundCallback: true` (`:560-566`). It also asserts the URL delivered to `openBrowser` is the nonce/challenge-carrying authorize URL and that the PKCE verifier never appears in it (`:536-546`).

2. `packages/cli/test/login-command.test.ts` runs the *real* command action end-to-end via `program.parseAsync(['node','wafflebase','--server',SERVER,'login'])` (`:84-95`), with only `open` and the session file mocked at their real boundaries, then takes the URL actually passed to `open()` (`:24-29`, `:138-149`), fetches the real loopback callback with the nonce from that URL, and asserts the exchange happened with `granted-code` and that a forged `state` gets 403 (`:135-209`). So a leak of the wrong value into `open()`, or a nonce mismatch between URL and listener, would fail these tests rather than pass.

Only a narrow residual gap remains (no end-to-end parse of the literal `--allow-unbound-callback` flag string through commander's camel-casing), which is not the claim made and is at most minor.

No test triggers the 30s timeout: login-callback.test.ts uses only `settledWithin(..., 50)` (which resolves to `null` on non-settlement) and never installs fake timers, and `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` is asserted only as a 400 response body (line ~99), never as the rejection reason. The version-skew signal the doc comment calls the point of the design is therefore untested.

verdict.reason:
The finding's premise does not hold in this repository, and the behavior it says is untested is in fact covered by real timeout tests.

1) The described code does not exist. `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` and `sawUnboundCallback` appear nowhere in the repo (grep across the whole tree: no matches). packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:373-385 is `nonceMatches`'s tail plus the `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS` doc comment — not a branch on `sawUnboundCallback`. The actual mechanism is `lastRefusal` (login.ts:520,530) fed into `loginTimeoutMessage(refusal)` (login.ts:460-463) at the timeout rejection (login.ts:656-666). The cited test file `packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts` does not exist at all (Glob `**/login-callback*` → no files).

2) The equivalent behavior IS tested, with the real timer firing. `startCallbackServer` exposes a `timeoutMs` seam (login.ts:475-476, 666), and packages/cli/test/login.test.ts drives it:
- test/login.test.ts:327-339 "names the missing state when the timeout is reached": sends a state-less callback (expects 403), then asserts the *rejection* of `waitForCallback()` matches /no `state`/ and /older than this CLI/ — i.e. exactly the nonce-less-callback signal instead of the generic timeout message.
- test/login.test.ts:356-371 asserts the plain timeout message and EXIT_USER_ERROR when nothing was refused, giving the contrasting branch.
- test/login.test.ts:401-426 asserts the refused state-less callback never makes the message prescribe `--allow-unbound-callback`, and 428-447 covers the mismatched-state variant; 341-354 covers non-GET.
These use a real 150/300ms timeout rather than fake timers, so no `useFakeTimers` is needed and the reviewer's search terms could not have found them.

Both the symbol/file the finding rests on and the claimed coverage gap are absent from this repo.

finding.summary: No test covers login.ts's actual hand-off: that `open()` and stderr receive `startUrl` and not the nonce-bearing URL
finding.evidence: The test titled 'keeps the nonce out of the URL handed to the browser and to stderr' (test line 184) only inspects the `startUrl` string returned by `startCallbackServer` and the `/start` redirect. It never touches the login action handler, so the security property it names — login.ts:66-72 printing `startUrl` and passing `startUrl` (not `buildAuthorizeUrl(...)`) to `open()` — is untested: swapping line 67 or line 72 back to the nonce-carrying URL would break the stated guarantee with every test still green. The only test of the action-registering function (test line 226) asserts merely that the command and the `--allow-unbound-callback` option exist, which says nothing about the hand-off.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise does not exist in this repo: `startUrl` and `buildAuthorizeUrl` have zero matches repo-wide; login.ts:60-73 is the --allow-unbound-callback option registration, and login.ts:253-273 documents the deliberate OPPOSITE behavior (the nonce-bearing oauthUrl is intentionally printed to stderr and handed to openBrowser, because it is the only fallback when the browser cannot open, with the listener timeout bounding exposure). So there is no "keep the nonce out of the browser URL" property to cover. Separately, the coverage claimed missing exists twice. (1) packages/cli/test/login-command.test.ts mocks the `open` module (lines 24-29) and drives the REAL action handler via registerLoginCommand + program.parseAsync([...,'login']) (lines 85-93), then asserts on the exact URL open() received: origin, /auth/github, mode=cli, 64-hex nonce, positive port, PKCE challenge == sha256(verifier sent to exchange), and verifier absent from the query (lines 153-174); it further proves that URL's nonce is the one bound to the live loopback listener by fetching the real callback with it and requiring 200 (lines 141-148). (2) packages/cli/test/login.test.ts:463-546 drives runLogin with an injected openBrowser (lines 501-503) and asserts the URL handed to the browser carries nonce === listenerNonce (line 533) plus challenge-but-not-verifier (540-545). The reviewer's report of grepping for mocks of 'open' and finding none is wrong, and the cited file packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts does not exist (nor does any test titled 'keeps the nonce out of the URL handed to the browser and to stderr'). Both counterexample files are collected by packages/cli/vitest.config.ts:5.
